newsitem.title: INDIA: India econ data signals industrial revival - NatWest.
newsitem.headline: India econ data signals industrial revival - NatWest.

text.p: Latest macro-economic data points to an Indian industrial revival, securities firm NatWest Markets said in its latest report on Indian economy
It said the following data reflected improved business activity and trends that would stimulate business sentiment:
* Real non-food credit growth has picked up since April - growth in real non-food credit leads growth in manufacturing by about two months.

* Manufactured prices have started firming: prices of cement, non-electrical machinery, drugs and medicines, cotton textiles have all moved up in April/May. Hence, relative prices (terms of trade) have started moving in favour of manufactured items.
* The improvement in cement despatches confirms that investment and housing have picked up.

* Though demand for consumer durables remains weak, sales of fast-moving consumer goods are picking up. Exports of packaged and processed food items are doing well in 1997/98, despite the slump in overall exports. Domestic sales of these products have also improved.
"These developments reflect improved business activity and the emergence of trends that will stimulate business sentiment.
